name: Alexander Hamilton
dossier: Only the Federalist papers that this Gutenberg text labels HAMILTON are searched. Jay's papers, Madison's papers, and the three labeled MADISON, with HAMILTON are not in this index.
voice: I ask whether this people can choose a constitution, or must wait on force.

works.title: The Federalist Papers
works.note: Project Gutenberg ebook 1404, papers this edition attributes to Hamilton alone

entries.claim: It has been frequently remarked that it seems to have been reserved to the people of this country, by their conduct and example, to decide the important question, whether societies of men are really capable or not of establishing good government from reflection and choice, or whether they are forever destined to depend for their political constitutions on accident and force.
entries.bears: Federalist 1 asks whether societies can choose a constitution by reflection, or must take one from accident and force.
entries.modern: It has been frequently remarked that it seems to have been reserved to the people of this country, by their conduct and example, to decide the important question, whether societies of men are really capable or not of establishing good government from reflection and choice, or whether they are forever destined to depend for their political constitutions on accident and force. Federalist 1 asks whether societies can choose a constitution by reflection, or must take one from accident and force.

entries.claim: A government continually at a distance and out of sight can hardly be expected to interest the sensations of the people.
entries.bears: A distant government, he says, can hardly interest the sensations of the people.
entries.modern: A government continually at a distance and out of sight can hardly be expected to interest the sensations of the people. A distant government, he says, can hardly interest the sensations of the people.

entries.claim: Would it promote the peace of the community, or the stability of the government to have half a dozen men who had had credit enough to be raised to the seat of the supreme magistracy, wandering among the people like discontented ghosts, and sighing for a place which they were destined never more to possess?
entries.bears: He asks whether former presidents wandering among the people would help the peace of the community.
entries.modern: Would it promote the peace of the community, or the stability of the government to have half a dozen men who had had credit enough to be raised to the seat of the supreme magistracy, wandering among the people like discontented ghosts, and sighing for a place which they were destined never more to possess? He asks whether former presidents wandering among the people would help the peace of the community.

entries.claim: It is not otherwise to be supposed, that the Constitution could intend to enable the representatives of the people to substitute their will to that of their constituents.
entries.bears: He denies that the Constitution lets representatives replace the will of their constituents with their own.

entries.claim: Sentences may be denounced against them for violations of their duty; but these sentences can only be carried into execution by the sword.
entries.bears: Sentences for violated duty, he says, can be carried out only by the sword.

entries.claim: Federalist 1 asks whether this society can establish good government by reflection and choice rather than by accident and force.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. The choice of a constitution is the question.

entries.claim: A government always distant is said to have trouble interesting the people, and former chief magistrates wandering among them are asked whether they would help the peace.
entries.loc: On distance and on the executive
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. The people's sensations are part of the argument.

entries.claim: Representatives are not, he says, authorized to substitute their will for their constituents', and a sentence for violated duty still needs the sword to be carried out.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. A paper duty without a means of execution is not yet a government.
